q: What is CPT in the hybrid program and how much does the CPT course cost?
answer:
CPT (Curricular Practical Training) lets F-1 students gain work experience related to their major. The hybrid program requires it. Each hybrid student must secure an approved internship or employment and stay continuously enrolled in the CPT course each term [1].

**Cost:** The CPT course fee equals one credit hour of tuition per term [1][3]. The sources don't give the dollar amount. The tuition page asks students to contact gradinternational@belhaven.edu for current rates, and Belhaven can change fees and tuition [3].

Other hybrid CPT program costs include tuition, a resource fee, books, and a graduation audit fee [2][3].

As an F-1 student, keep these points in mind:
- Don't start working until you receive a CPT-authorized I-20 [4].
- CPT can't start before your program's first day and can't be backdated [4].
- Twelve or more months of full-time CPT at the same degree level makes you ineligible for OPT at that level [4].

Confirm your own situation with the DSO before acting. CPT questions go through the DSO ticket system: https://igsupport.belhaven.edu/open.php [7]. For tuition rates, contact gradinternational@belhaven.edu [3].

- **Timing:** The first week of classes is the Add/Drop period, and you can drop through Sunday of that week. [2] For online courses starting January 11, 2027, drops end January 17, 2027, and dropped classes aren't charged. [6]
- **After that week:** Dropping becomes a withdrawal through a Blazenet form, which can have financial, athletic and academic effects. [2] For those online courses, the last day to withdraw with a "W" is February 15, 2027. [6]
- **Advising:** Talk to your academic advisor and financial aid before dropping. [2]

Before you drop, confirm with the DSO that it won't affect your F-1 status. You can open a ticket at https://igsupport.belhaven.edu/open.php.

q: Are accommodations available for online students?
answer:
Yes. Students who qualify under the ADA can request reasonable accommodations through Student Care, which evaluates your documentation to determine them [3][4].

For online students:
- You need to renew your accommodation letter each semester you are enrolled [1].
- Accommodations are only put in place once your professors have the official letter. They are not retroactive, so request them early [1].
- Your documentation must include an evaluator's report with a specific diagnosis and severity, the approximate duration, and a description of past accommodations. A single test, an IEP or a 504 plan alone is not enough [2].
- Once your file is reviewed, Student Care will contact you to go over your letter [1].

The pages don't say whether online students have a separate request process or how long review takes, so confirm with Student Care.

Contact Student Care at 601-968-8865 or studentcare@belhaven.edu [7].

- **Fri, Dec. 4:** Tue/Thu 9:25, MWF 11:00 and 2:00 [5]

Most exams run 9-11 am, 12-2 pm or 3-5 pm. Check your syllabus for your exact date, time and location [3]. Final grades are due Dec. 9 [5].
